name: fixed-workflow-pilot-proxy-audit
pilot_family_coverage_note: No existing question is labelled for a pilot family: none carries a metadata count, a topic-match count, per-Record relevance labels, a Paper Chat scope or a named two-Record comparison. Fifteen are adaptable starting points, listed under adaptable_candidates, but each needs Record-level relevance labels before it can score a workflow. New pilot-family questions must be written; the 60-question, six-per-family, 30/30 design is an exploratory proposal and gives no per-category reliability at six examples.

presence_listing.why: 'which work/papers ...?' questions labelled with passages from the paper(s) that answer them. The labels name a paper, not a complete relevant set, so they can test whether that paper is among the candidates and say nothing about completeness. q26, q27, q28, q34 and q52 each label two papers; q108-q112 label one.

presence_with_no_expected_match.why: 'which paper in the repository ...?' questions labelled decline-no-evidence. Under the subset contract a workflow may say no assessed match was found among the candidates it screened; it may not claim the repository holds none.

split.rule: Every existing question is development. All 113 have been read while tuning retrieval and the evidence decision (IR-133, IR-394, IR-463-467, IR-481-486), so none can serve as held-out evidence. Held-out membership is empty until new questions are written by someone who does not tune on them.
